decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 2%. The vote was 8-2. Dissenting: Richard W. Fisher, Charles I. Plosser.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 2 percent.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 2 percent.
Financial markets remain under considerable stress, and tight credit conditions and the deepening housing contraction are likely to weigh on economic growth over the next few quarters.
The Committee will continue to monitor economic and financial developments and will act as needed to promote sustainable economic growth and price stability.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.75% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.77% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.88% would fall by about $15.31 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 5.1%, and employers added an average of -45k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4% over the past year (March 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.02% on the day.
